title: The development of summary judgment
summary: The assigned history traces movement from narrow collection procedures and cautious use toward the broader role associated with the 1986 trilogy. Competing concerns involve unnecessary trials, jury protection, cost, and access to proof.
notes: The earlier slightest-doubt approach is not the later trilogy’s standard. The casebook’s critical commentary about increased use should remain identifiable as commentary.

sections.Meaning: The assigned history traces movement from narrow collection procedures and cautious use toward the broader role associated with the 1986 trilogy. Competing concerns involve unnecessary trials, jury protection, cost, and access to proof.
sections.How to work through the question: Compare the Frank–Clark debate in Arnstein, the caution in Poller, and the burdens and evidentiary approach in Celotex, Anderson, and Matsushita. Distinguish historical language from the test being applied in the later cases.
